blocks.prompt: 12. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(x\sin x\,dx + \ln y\,dy = 0\).
blocks.explanation:
The variables are already separated: \(x\) only with \(dx\), \(y\) only with \(dy\).
Plan: integrate each term; both integrals need integration by parts.
steps:
Given: \(x\sin x\,dx + \ln y\,dy = 0\), \(y > 0\).
To find: the general solution.
Method: separable (already separated). Integrate term by term; use integration by parts \(\int u\,dv = uv - \int v\,du\) for \(\int x\sin x\,dx\) and \(\int\ln y\,dy\).

Write the integrals
\[\int x\sin x\,dx + \int\ln y\,dy = C\]
Why: integrate both terms; the integral of 0 is a constant.

First integral (\(u = x\), \(dv = \sin x\,dx\))
\[\int x\sin x\,dx = -x\cos x + \int\cos x\,dx\]
\[= -x\cos x + \sin x\]
Why: \(du = dx\), \(v = -\cos x\); choosing \(u = x\) makes it simpler after differentiating.

Second integral (\(u = \ln y\), \(dv = dy\))
\[\int\ln y\,dy = y\ln y - \int y \cdot \dfrac{1}{y}\,dy\]
\[= y\ln y - y\]
Why: \(du = \frac{1}{y}\,dy\), \(v = y\).

Combine
\[-x\cos x + \sin x + y\ln y - y = C\]
\[y\ln y = y + x\cos x - \sin x + C\]
Why: move every term except \(y\ln y\) to the right side.

Check
Differentiate \(y\ln y - y - x\cos x + \sin x = C\):
\[(\ln y + 1)\dfrac{dy}{dx} - \dfrac{dy}{dx} - \cos x + x\sin x + \cos x = 0\]
\[\ln y\dfrac{dy}{dx} + x\sin x = 0\]
Multiply by \(dx\): the given equation.
blocks.final_answer: \(y\ln y = y + x\cos x - \sin x + C\)
